record.paper_title: Positive and free boundary solutions to singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption: an overview and open problems
record.original_question: For the star-shaped-domain problem −Δu + u^α = λu^β in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω, 0 < α < β < 1, and N > 2(1+α)(1+β)/((1−α)(1−β)), Ilyasov and Egorov construct a positive solution w_λ > 0 satisfying ∂w_λ/∂n ≠ 0 on ∂Ω. Must this first solution in fact satisfy the sign condition ∂w_λ/∂n ≤ 0 on ∂Ω?

evidence.quote: (i) there exists a solution wλ > 0 such that ∂wλ/∂n 6= 0 on ∂Ω,
One could think that in the first case we actually have ∂wλ/∂n ≤ 0 on ∂Ω and in the second uλ > 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$ which is star-shaped with respect to some interior point, and let $n$ denote the outward unit normal to $\partial\Omega$. Fix exponents $0 < \alpha < \beta < 1$ satisfying the dimensional condition
$$N > \frac{2(1+\alpha)(1+\beta)}{(1-\alpha)(1-\beta)},$$
and let $\lambda > 0$ be a parameter. Consider the singular semilinear elliptic boundary value problem
$$-\Delta u + u^{\alpha} = \lambda\, u^{\beta} \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega,$$
seeking nonnegative weak solutions $u$ that are positive in $\Omega$ and whose normal derivative $\partial u/\partial n$ exists on $\partial\Omega$ in the appropriate sense.

Suppose $w_\lambda$ is a positive solution of this problem (constructed for suitable $\lambda$) satisfying the property that $\partial w_\lambda/\partial n$ does not vanish identically on $\partial\Omega$ (i.e. $\partial w_\lambda/\partial n \not\equiv 0$).

Question: Must such a solution $w_\lambda$ necessarily satisfy the sign condition
$$\frac{\partial w_\lambda}{\partial n} \le 0 \quad \text{on } \partial\Omega\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: No specific resolution of this conjectural sign property for the first positive solution $w_\lambda$ of the singular absorption problem $-\Delta u + u^\alpha = \lambda u^\beta$ on star-shaped domains was located in available sources. The problem is posed as an open question in the surrounding literature and no later work confirming or refuting the sign condition $\partial w_\lambda/\partial n \le 0$ on $\partial\Omega$ was found.
